markets.question: Will Wages Beat Inflation in 2026?
markets.description:
This market will settle to Yes if the 12-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls, seasonally adjusted, from December 2025 to December 2026, as reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in the Real Earnings release for December 2026, is greater than 0.0 percent. Outcome sourced from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

This market settles based on the Real Earnings release published monthly alongside the Consumer Price Index, viewable at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/realer.toc.htm. Each month's figure is taken as first published; later revisions will not be considered.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics does not publish the 12-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for December 2026 by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will settle based on the 12-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for the most recent month prior to December 2026 for which it has been published.

For full rules, see: https://www.polymarketexchange.com/files/products/PMUS%20-%20RAHEC%20-%20(2026.10.06).pdf
markets.title: Yes

markets.question: Will Union Membership Rise in 2027?
markets.description:
This market will settle to Yes if the annual average number of wage and salary workers age 16 and over who were members of unions in 2027, as reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in the Union Members release for 2027, is greater than the number reported for 2026 in the Union Members release for 2026. Outcome sourced from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

This market settles based on the Union Members release published annually, viewable at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/union2.toc.htm. The number of union members is currently reported in thousands in Table 1 of each release. Each year's figure is taken as first published; later revisions will not be considered.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics does not publish the figure for 2026 or 2027 by March 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, the figure for the most recent year published prior to the missing year will be used in its place.

For full rules, see: https://www.polymarketexchange.com/files/products/PMUS%20-%20UNMBC%20-%20(2026.10.06).pdf
markets.title: Yes

markets.question: How Many US Homes Built in 2026?
markets.description:
This market will settle to Yes if the estimated annual total of privately-owned housing units completed in the United States for 2026, as reported by the U.S. Census Bureau in the New Residential Construction release for December 2026, is greater than or equal to 1,400,000. Outcome sourced from the U.S. Census Bureau.

This market settles based on the estimated annual total of privately-owned housing units completed (not seasonally adjusted), published in the U.S. Census Bureau's New Residential Construction release, currently in Table 5b, viewable at https://www.census.gov/construction/nrc/index.html. Each year's figure is taken as first published; later revisions will not be considered.

If the U.S. Census Bureau does not publish the estimated annual total of privately-owned housing units completed for 2026 by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will settle based on the estimated annual total of privately-owned housing units completed for the most recent year prior to 2026 for which it has been published.

For full rules, see: https://www.polymarketexchange.com/files/products/PMUS%20-%20HUCMC%20-%20(2026.10.06).pdf
